acceptance: The gate report counts cells whose returned order was verified versus compared unordered, per benchmark
ORDER BY ALL is checked by expanding to all output columns; qualified columns that unambiguously match one output column are resolved
DECIMAL sort keys keep exact precision in the key table
Tests cover each shape, including a mis-ordered result that must fail
context: Raised by the agy and muse adversarial reviews (2026-10-04). Evaluation errors now fail closed (#2621).
description: The derived ORDER BY check in benchbox/core/equivalence/cross_surface.py (_derived_order_violation) falls back to the unordered comparison when the output has duplicate column names, a sort term uses a qualified column (t.x), a term has no column reference (DuckDB ORDER BY ALL), or a term references a non-projected column. DECIMAL keys are compared as DOUBLE, which can merge distinct keys above about 1e13. These fallbacks are silent: the gate report does not say which cells had their order verified.
